summary:
# NOTES: RUTH FIELDING AT GOLDEN PASS (Alice B. Emerson, Cupples & Leon, 1925)

Single book. Series: Ruth Fielding #21. Also front/back matter lists other series (Ruth Fielding list, Betty Gordon, Barton, Linger-Not, Billie Bradley, Curlytops). Ads only; no story content.

## Characters
- **Ruth Fielding**: orphan, Red Mill near Cheslow; scenario writer/director, Fielding Film Corp. Lived with Great-uncle Jabez Potter and Aunt Alvirah Boggs (calls Ruth "my pretty").
- **Uncle Jabez Potter**: crabbed, disapproves of Ruth's pictures; face "like a nut cracker" (Jennie).
- **Aunt Alvirah Boggs**: sweet, eccentric housekeeper, frail, quick dark eyes, back/bones ache.
- **Helen Cameron**: Ruth's chum, Tom's twin; engaged to Chess Copley.
- **Tom Cameron**: Helen's twin, Ruth's business partner; secretly jealous of Layton Boardman; loves Ruth.
- **Chess Copley**: Helen's fiancé; uncle backs his business deal ("snowball property" up North).
- **Jennie Marchand** ("Heavy," née Stone): married to Henri Marchand, French; round face, jolly.
- **Ann Hicks**: wants to be extra; "bust bronchos."
- **Mercy Curtis**: lives in Cheslow.
- **Mary Cox** ("The Fox"); **Nettie Parsons**; **Barclay Clayton** ("Bark," Ruth's escort).
- **Mr. Hammond**: president, Alectrion Film Corp.; accepted Ruth's "The Heart of a School Girl"; suggests Ruth act; recommended Headwaters Ranch.
- **Layton Boardman**: western actor, big, black hair, dark gray long eyes, quiet wit, skilled rider/roper; ex-Palatial Films (quarreled with Sol Bloomberg). Signed to hero for "Hearts of the Mountains." Injured (ankle, back, head) when thrown by colt. Confesses to Tom he is "no lady's man," only acted love.
- **Viola Callahan**: temperamental star; ex-Brennan contract (threw it at manager); Ruth signed her at high salary. Former love of Tony Martano. Deserts to Sol Bloomberg with Tony.
- **Anita Townsend, Grand**: co-stars of "Snowblind."
- **Sol Bloomberg**: chief owner, Palatial Films; enemy of Boardman; sends agent **Charlie Reid** to meet Viola in Chicago.
- **Dave Sentner**: comedian. **Shepley**: tall thin director, Ruth's right hand. Two cameramen, two assistant directors; old deaf trapper character man.
- **Ma and Pa Gowdy**: Headwaters Ranch owners; Ma tall, calico, silent, grave. **Andy**: gangling youth, general utility. Mexican cooks. Foreman: long, lean, blue-eyed.
- **Edith Lang**: former star, Red Cross WWI decorated, leg lost to blood poisoning; coaches Ruth in acting.

## Places
Cheslow (Main Street, Palace theater, Cheslow hotel); Red Mill; Briarwood Hall; Golden Pass, Montana; Headwaters Ranch (between mountains, stream); Chicago hotel; Golden Pass station (dismal, deserted).

## Events in order
**Ch I – Fire:** Premiere of "Snowblind" at the Palace, Cheslow. Ruth fears audience reaction. Helen teasing. Surprise party arrives singing Briarwood yell ("Sweetbriars all-l!...S.B.—Ah-h-h!...Briarwood Hall! That's all!"). Ruth hugs friends. Mrs. Jennie Marchand and Ann Hicks organized. Uncle Jabez grumbles. Ruth speaks on stage; explosion; lights out; smoke.

**Ch II – Tom to the Rescue:** Panic. Ruth trapped behind stage in smoke. Chess with Helen; Uncle Jabez: "Somebody's got to get ahold o' that girl!" Aunt Alvirah: "Somebody go find my pretty." Tom reaches Ruth, leads her through door: "Safe, Ruth, safe!" Backstory: Ruth's adventures; Tom admires her; Helen-Chess romance.

**Ch III – Good Old Times:** Ruth reunited with Aunt Alvirah. Firemen; film storeroom explosion, smoke only. Chess hungry. Party at Cheslow hotel; Ruth guest of honor. Mr. Hammond arrives; mentions Golden Pass.

**Ch IV – Golden Pass:** Hammond praises picture; says Golden Pass, Montana is ideal (he visited for cattle round-up). Helen: "Montana! Whoop--ee!" Ruth plans western picture. Party breaks up; Ruth says "It is a good old world." Next day Boardman arrives (card via Aunt Alvirah). Ruth hires him.

**Ch V – A New Star:** Contract signed (Aunt Alvirah witnesses). Tom reluctant; objects ("too good looking to be honest"), mentions Bloomberg. Helen and Jennie arrive with news.

**Ch VI – Fine News:** Helen's news: Chess's uncle backing business deal; wedding will follow. Tom teases, Helen throws pillow. Tom locks away Ruth's manuscript; takes her driving.

**Ch VII – The Leading Lady:** "Snowblind" successful in cities. Chums visit; Jennie chaperones. Ruth hires Viola Callahan (Viola's rage at Brennan; Tony Martano confession; "Jealousy!"). Ruth distrusts Viola.

**Ch VIII – The Party:** Tom and Ruth quarrel over Viola's salary. Party night: Boardman attends, dances; Tom guards Ruth ("watch my step"). Friends leave next day from Cheslow station ("stay a year").

**Ch IX – On the Road:** Departure for Montana. Aunt Alvirah tearful; Uncle Jabez: "before they was dead and buried." Jennie leaves in Chicago ("two months in America"). Tom leads Chicago taxis. Ruth: "Adventure's in the air."

**Ch X – A Suspicious Move:** Company gathered (Dave Sentner, Shepley, cameramen). Helen asks about Boardman; Ruth defends him. Next morning Ruth and Helen see Viola talking secretly with Charlie Reid (Bloomberg's agent) in Chicago; Viola darts away.

**Ch XI – Trouble in the Air:** Train to Golden Pass; station. Boardman tames colt; "Seems like he's mine." Tom jealous. Scenic ride to Headwaters Ranch; Ma and Pa Gowdy. Ruth and Helen's rooms. Tom goes hunting with rifle; Ruth annoyed. Ruth rides out; stampede of steers.

**Ch XII – In Peril:** Ruth frozen in path. Boardman rides to save her; pony throws him, ankle/head injured. Tom and cowboys shoot; steers divide. Tom: "I couldn't have done anything else."

**Ch XIII – New Worries:** Helen and Ruth talk; avalanche planned (dynamite, artificial). Ruth visits Boardman in bed; Tom sees hands together, walks off.

**Ch XIV – Helen Is Hurt:** Boardman's injuries (ankle sprain, back, bruises). Rodeo planned (bronco busting, steer roping). Viola sneers at Boardman. Rodeo filmed; cowboy with real cartridge shoots; Helen struck (wound on forehead) and falls.

**Ch XV – Startling News:** Ruth's Red Cross training; Ma Gowdy helps; Helen recovers. Ruth finds Viola gone; note: "Sorry, but Tony and I are going over to Bloomberg... You will have to get some one in my place."

**Ch XVI – An Incredible Suggestion:** Mr. Hammond arrives by car; Ruth tells Tom and Hammond. Hammond suggests Ruth act herself.

**Ch XVII – Ruth Decides:** Helen enthusiastic; Tom opposes (jealousy over Boardman's lovemaking). Tom: "If I could be sure it was all just play acting!" Ruth decides: "Yes!"

**Ch XVIII – A New Role:** Ruth examines her face; screen tests succeed; Boardman praises her. Hammond recommends Edith Lang.

**Ch XIX – A New Friend:** Edith Lang arrives (artificial leg, limp); praises "Snowblind"; coaches Ruth ("twist the corners of the apron"). Tom goes to water hole, meets bear; Ruth finds him ("cowgirl... revolver at her belt").

**Ch XX – Not Acting:** Bear incident (bear lies on rock; Tom sits still; two-human stare sends it away).

**Ch XXI – The Narrow Ledge:** Avalanche location: mountain above deserted cabins. Ruth slips off ledge; Tom climbs down to ledge (~15 ft), catches Ruth. Boardman fetches rope.

**Ch XXII – A Test of Courage:** Ruth lets go; Tom catches her. Boardman lassoes; both rescued. Tom carries Ruth on horse. Avalanche day. Ruth in cave with company; Tom keeps hand on hers.

**Ch XXIII – Buried Alive:** Avalanche (planned) then unplanned second explosion (leftover dynamite house). Cave sealed. Tom explores tunnels, finds light.

**Ch XXIV – Bears:** Outside: Helen cries; Edith Lang comforts her; Hammond digs. Inside: Tom leads group through tunnel; two bears in second cave.

**Ch XXV – Sunlight Once More:** Boardman and Tom shoot bears (one dies, bear raked Tom's arm). Ruth makes tourniquet with twig from her skirt. Tom survives (old doctor praises Ruth). Cameras kept grinding. Chess arrives; Business good. Boardman tells Tom he is no lady's man. Tom: "I've been seven kinds of a fool." Ruth: "Wait just a little while, Tommy-boy."

**Epilogue:** "Hearts of the Mountains" premieres in New York; Ruth lifted to stage. Viola/Tony picture fails; Bloomberg disgraced. Helen envies Ruth; "the world at your feet, to say nothing of Tom!"

## Key quotes
- "Safe, Ruth, safe!" (Tom)
- "It is a good old world, isn't it, Auntie?"
- "Adventure's in the air."
- "Sorry, but Tony and I are going over to Bloomberg."
- "If I could be sure it was all just play acting!" (Tom, muttered)
- "Light! I see daylight!" (Tom)
- "Bears!... Two of them!"
